Red flags: 2024 to 2025 dispute over removing the Knickerbocker Greys cadet group from the armory
- Governor Kathy Hochul signed a state law in December 2024, sponsored by State Senator Liz Krueger and State Assemblyman Alex Bores, that bars the Park Avenue Armory Conservancy from evicting the Knickerbocker Greys, a cadet group founded in 1881, and lets it keep its roughly 800-square-foot basement space (West Side Spirit, Jack Ahern, 29 September 2025).
- The Seventh Regiment Armory Conservancy, which holds a 99-year state lease granted in 2006, filed a federal lawsuit against New York State on 5 September 2025 in Manhattan federal court, saying the cadets' use of the room would interfere with its $73 million basement renovation plan and calling the bill "a clear abuse of legislative power" (New York Post via AOL, Gabrielle Fahmy, 13 September 2025).
- The Conservancy argues the law violates the Contracts Clause, the Takings Clause and its due process rights, and calls it a "targeted political favor" obtained through lobbying (West Side Spirit, 29 September 2025).
- David Menegon, commandant of the Greys, said the group teaches "leadership, empathy, and confidence"; parents quoted called the suit baffling and said it punishes children (West Side Spirit, 29 September 2025).
- On 25 November 2025 Judge George B. Daniels of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York granted a preliminary injunction barring Empire State Development from enforcing the law, finding the Conservancy more likely than not to succeed on its Contracts Clause claim (Loeb & Loeb, counsel to the Conservancy, 3 December 2025).
